I've attached Recorded Crime per 10,000 residents (first half 2013) data for 33 London boroughs and a list showing which boroughs are geographic neighbors of each other.

Question: You can use a statistical method such as Getis-Ord Gi*, or any other method you choose, to identify boroughs where there is an unusually intense CONCENTRATION of high Recorded Crime per 10,000 residents (first half 2013) (a HOT spot) or low Recorded Crime per 10,000 residents (first half 2013) (a COLD spot), considering each borough TOGETHER WITH its neighbors as one combined local area.

This is different from asking whether a borough simply resembles its immediate neighbors -- instead, you are testing whether the COMBINED total (the borough together with its neighbors) is unusually large or small compared to the citywide average, regardless of how similar the borough is to any one neighbor individually.

Note: a borough whose own value is missing should not itself be reported as a hot or cold spot in your final answer. Note: dedicated spatial-statistics packages (pysal, esda, libpysal, geopandas, or similar) are NOT installed in this environment -- don't spend turns trying different import paths for them. Implement your chosen method directly using only pandas and numpy. If your method produces a z-score, use the standard critical values: |z| > 1.96 for 95% confidence, |z| > 2.576 for 99% confidence.

End your response with exactly one line listing every borough you identified, using HOT for hot spot and COLD for cold spot, and including the computed real number (e.g. a z-score) for each:
FINAL ANSWER: BoroughName1 (HOT, z-score = <value>), BoroughName2 (COLD, z-score = <value>), ... (z-score is just an example label -- if your method produces a different statistic, use its name instead, but the value after '=' must be a real number)

If you find none, write: FINAL ANSWER: none

Dataset path (read-only): chunks_csv/getisord/getisord_crime_first_half_2013.csv
IMPORTANT -- two rules that are easy to get wrong, read carefully:
1. STATELESS: each ```python``` block runs in its own fresh process with NO memory of variables, imports, or dataframes from earlier blocks. Every single block must start from scratch: re-import pandas/numpy if you use them by name, and reload the dataset (df = pd.read_csv(DATASET_PATH)) even if you already loaded it in a previous block. Referencing a variable from an earlier block will fail with NameError.
2. ALWAYS print() what you want to see. This is NOT a notebook -- writing a bare variable name or expression at the end of a script (e.g. `Q1, Q3, IQR`) produces NO visible output here, unlike Jupyter. Every value you want to check or use as evidence must be wrapped in print(), e.g. print('Q1:', Q1). pandas and numpy are pre-imported as pd and np. If you want to save a chart or file, save it into ARTIFACTS_DIR (already defined), never elsewhere.

Every single message you send MUST start with a line beginning 'Thought:' -- a message with a ```python``` block but no preceding Thought line is not valid ReAct format and will be rejected.

Thought: I need to load the crime data and adjacency data, check for missing values, build the adjacency list, compute local sums, calculate z-scores, and identify hot/cold spots.

Action:
```python
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

DATASET_PATH = 'chunks_csv/getisord/getisord_crime_first_half_2013.csv'
ADJACENCY_PATH = 'chunks_csv/borough_adjacency.csv'

# Load crime data and drop rows with missing values
crime_df = pd.read_csv(DATASET_PATH)
crime_df = crime_df.dropna(subset=['crime_rate_value'])

# Load adjacency data
adj_df = pd.read_csv(ADJACENCY_PATH)

# Create a mapping from borough to crime rate
crime_rates = crime_df.set_index('borough')['crime_rate_value']

# Build bidirectional adjacency list for valid boroughs
valid_boroughs = set(crime_df['borough'])
neighbors_dict = {}

for _, row in adj_df.iterrows():
    borough = row['borough']
    neighbor = row['neighbor']
    if borough in valid_boroughs and neighbor in valid_boroughs:
        if borough not in neighbors_dict:
            neighbors_dict[borough] = set()
        neighbors_dict[borough].add(neighbor)
        if neighbor not in neighbors_dict:
            neighbors_dict[neighbor] = set()
        neighbors_dict[neighbor].add(borough)

# Compute local sums (borough + neighbors)
local_sums = {}
for borough in crime_rates.index:
    neighbors = neighbors_dict.get(borough, set())
    neighbor_rates = [crime_rates[neighbor] for neighbor in neighbors if neighbor in crime_rates]
    total = crime_rates[borough] + sum(neighbor_rates)
    local_sums[borough] = total

# Calculate z-scores
local_sums_array = np.array(list(local_sums.values()))
mean_local_sum = np.mean(local_sums_array)
std_local_sum = np.std(local_sums_array, ddof=1)  # Sample standard deviation

z_scores = {}
for borough, total in local_sums.items():
    z = (total - mean_local_sum) / std_local_sum
    z_scores[borough] = z

# Identify hot and cold spots
hot_spots = {b: z for b, z in z_scores.items() if z > 1.96}
cold_spots = {b: z for b, z in z_scores.items() if z < -1.96}

print("Hot spots:", hot_spots)
print("Cold spots:", cold_spots)
print("Mean local sum:", mean_local_sum)
print("Std local sum:", std_local_sum)
```
